body:
The research proposed a column-major copy of the feature matrix so the presort split-finder gather x[order[k]][f] reads a contiguous column instead of chasing a row pointer per sample. The sizing argument was checked and correct: the payload is 4000 by 20 by 8 bytes plus 4000 row headers, past the M2 Pro 128 KB L1, while one column is 32 KB and L1-resident.

IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED: BenchmarkTreeFit -3.7 percent, BenchmarkGBMFit +0.25 percent. Reverted.

WHY THE ESTIMATE WAS HIGH: the gather is already hoisted once per node. The comment at the site records an earlier optimization that halved it — the inline form re-gathered every value TWICE across adjacent sweep iterations, and hoisting into a per-node vals buffer removed that. What remains is one gather per sample per candidate feature per node, and the sweep that consumes vals sequentially dominates it. Relayout helps a gather that is the loop; here the gather is the prologue.

A CORRECTNESS TRAP FOUND ON THE WAY, worth recording for any future attempt: cartBuilder is constructed on TWO paths. initColumns is the presort path, but RandomForestClassifier.Fit builds per-tree builders that never call it, so a field initialized only there is empty under the forest and the first sweep panics with an index out of range. Any per-builder derived state has to be initialized where x is set, not where the columns are.

The six static equal-chunk row loops and the SVM per-element non-inlinable kernel call from the same sweep remain unmeasured and are the better candidates in this package.

body:
The research proposed hoisting the loop-invariant kernel switch out of kernelCache.column, where m.kernel was called once per sample and re-took the switch each time inside a method that can never inline (its arms contain loops). The argument was sound on its face: 4000 non-inlinable calls per materialized column, up to 2048 columns per fit.

IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED: BenchmarkSVCFit/n4000_rbf 6717273 to 6896458 ns/op, +2.7 percent — SLOWER. Reverted.

WHY: the column fill is not where the time goes at this shape. Each element is 20 subtract-multiply-adds plus a math.Exp, so the call overhead the hoist removes is a small fraction of the body it wraps, and specializing the loop apparently cost more than the indirection saved. The SMO iteration that consumes the columns dominates.

RECORD FOR THE PACKAGE-LEVEL CLAIM: this was named as the route to closing the 2.0x RBF-SVC gap against sklearn. It is not — that gap is elsewhere, and the next attempt should profile the SMO loop rather than the kernel evaluation.

Still unmeasured in this package: the six static equal-chunk row-parallel loops, which are now the only remaining candidate from that sweep.

SHIPPED. nbPredictParallel dealt one equal chunk per worker and joined at a barrier; rows are now claimed from an atomic cursor in blocks of 256. BenchmarkGaussianNBPredict -5.4 percent, and -5.7 percent with the arms measured in the reverse order.

THE DIAGNOSTICS CAME FIRST AND EXPLAIN THE SIZE OF THE NUMBER. The forced-serial control shows the chunker IS on the hot path — forcing it serial costs 2.7x — so the loop is genuinely parallel-dominated and the candidate was worth pursuing. But the GOMAXPROCS sweep is MONOTONIC (4: 108126, 8: 100030, 12: 92663 ns/op): more cores are faster, which is exactly the signal PS3011 says separates an efficiency-core imbalance, where more cores get SLOWER, from ordinary imperfect scaling. Claiming fixes imbalance, so with no imbalance to fix the win is small. 2.7x on twelve cores also says most of the scaling loss is elsewhere — bandwidth or per-worker overhead rather than scheduling — which is where the next attempt on this package should look.

Both PS3011 preconditions hold here, which is why claiming pays at all: a claim working set is the rows it covers, and the body allocates nothing per call.

THE GATE FIRST FIXTURE PROVED NOTHING AND MUTATION SAID SO. The helper runs serial below n*feat = 8192 and the first sizes (13, 300, 1027 rows at 6 features) were all under it, so the test compared the serial path against itself; a mutation SKIPPING a row per claim passed. At 4000 and 5003 rows the parallel arm is entered and that mutation reddens. Cast as rule A-PARALLEL-GATE-MUST-CLEAR-THE-SERIAL-THRESHOLD-001. Overlapping claims still do not redden it, correctly: recomputing a pure per-row write changes nothing.

FIVE SIBLING LOOPS REMAIN unconverted (knn, gbm predict, forest, svm decision, dbscan). Each needs its own screen — the NB result says a monotonic sweep predicts a small win, so screen before converting rather than assuming the shape transfers.

txt: WHEN a loop reads one column of a [][]T at a data-dependent row, x[idx[k]][f], and the same column is re-read many times, the owner of that matrix SHALL mirror it feature-major once where it is already walked and read the mirror, accepting the n*d element memory cost and gating the change with a bit-exact digest.

WHEN a type whose initializer allocates 3 or more buffers is constructed once per work item, the that initializer SHALL take the buffers from a sync.Pool, growing each only when the pooled one is too small, and return them when the item finishes.

WHEN looking for unused parallelism and the per-item work lives inside a CALLEE rather than in an inner loop, the reviewer SHALL check single loops too, because every nest-based check requires a depth of 2 or more and cannot see this shape.

WHEN a serial reduction with a first-wins tie rule is replaced by a chunked parallel one, the test suite SHALL pin the tie rule with a fixture that MANUFACTURES a tie, in both placements, rather than relying on an output digest.

WHEN a serial loop keeping a running best over independent items is chunked across workers, the implementer SHALL apply the same strict comparison within each chunk and then fold the chunks in ASCENDING order with that same comparison, so the serial winner is reproduced exactly including ties.
